_how: The answer key for scripts/truth-test.js: buildings that actually SOLD, with the closed price. THE TRUTH FILE IS THE TEST. Key every figure from the public record or the page that states it, never from a CompNinja report, or the scorecard grades the tool against itself. Only sales whose price is PUBLIC belong in this file, because it is committed; a closed deal whose price is not public goes in truth-set.private.json (git-ignored; start it with: node scripts/truth-test.js --init-private). Single properties only, arms-length, closed: no portfolios, auctions, foreclosures, ground leases, partial interests, or asking prices. Changing or removing an entry breaks comparison with older runs in docs/evals, so add rather than edit.

_fields.id: short, lowercase, unique, never reused: elgin-ind-01
_fields.address: 123 Main St, City, ST 12345 (must start with the street number and end City, ST)
_fields.type: Industrial | Office | Retail | Multifamily | Land | Residential
_fields.sale_price: the CLOSED price as a plain number: 5250000. Leave it and sale_date out for a building that has not closed yet; its prediction is stored, and filling them in later scores it with --rescore
_fields.size_sqft: building square feet (the lot, for Land). Optional, but without it the size lookup cannot be graded
_fields.source: the page or record that states the price
_fields.checked: true once a person has opened the source and confirmed price, address, size and date
_fields.months: optional: a lookback window other than that type's default
_fields.note: anything a careful reader should know
